title: The IB Study Platform Top Scorers Actually Use
summary: See what makes an IB study platform effective for top scorers, from exam-style practice and feedback to honest evidence about RevisionDojo.
body_markdown:
An **IB study platform for top scorers** should do more than store notes and display questions. It should help students identify weaknesses, practise under realistic conditions, receive useful feedback, and repeat that process across six subjects and the Diploma Programme core.


RevisionDojo is designed around this complete study cycle. Its main distinction is the connection between syllabus-aligned explanations, active recall, exam-style questions, answer feedback, timed practice, and coursework support. This article examines those tools, the evidence behind them, and the limitations students and parents should understand.


### What top IB scores actually require


A score of **45 points** comes from six subject grades of 7 plus the maximum three core points:


6×7+3=456 \\times 7 + 3 = 45

The IB awards grades from 1-7 in each subject. Theory of knowledge and the extended essay can contribute up to three additional points, while CAS must be completed but does not add points.


This structure explains why top performance requires more than subject knowledge. Students must manage calculations, essays, data analysis, oral work, internal assessments, and timed examinations. An isolated mathematics website or folder of biology notes may help, but neither provides a complete Diploma Programme system.


Students aiming for 40-45 points generally need four connected processes:


- **Understanding:** learning concepts accurately and at the required syllabus depth
- **Retention:** recalling definitions, formulas, examples, quotations, and methods
- **Application:** responding effectively to IB command terms and unfamiliar questions
- **Evaluation:** diagnosing lost marks and correcting the underlying weakness


The best IB resource is therefore not necessarily the one containing the most material. It is the one that makes these processes easy to repeat.


### What separates serious IB tools from basic resources


Many students rely on generic videos, shared notes, broad AI chatbots, or random question collections. These may explain individual ideas, but students must still check syllabus relevance, find suitable practice, interpret marking expectations, and record weaknesses.


A stronger platform reduces this friction without removing intellectual effort. The student must still produce answers, justify reasoning, and evaluate feedback.

Familiarity is not mastery. Reading polished explanations can create confidence without proving that a student can retrieve and apply the idea independently. Dunlosky and colleagues rated **practice testing** and **distributed practice** as high-utility learning strategies, supporting tools built around retrieval, repetition, and correction.


### How RevisionDojo supports top-scoring IB study


RevisionDojo connects its resources within subject pages instead of treating notes, questions, and feedback as unrelated products. Its[platform overview](https://www.revisiondojo.com/help-center/what-is-revisiondojo) explains how students can move among Questionbank practice, Study Notes, interactive lessons, Flashcards, past-paper walkthroughs, and coursework tools.


### Syllabus-aligned learning and recall


[RevisionDojo's IB resource library](https://www.revisiondojo.com/ib) organizes notes, questions, flashcards, videos, study guides, and worked examples by subject. This provides a structured starting point when classroom teaching was unclear or a topic needs to be relearned.


Notes alone are insufficient for top-level performance. After reading a section, students should close it and reconstruct the main argument, process, or derivation from memory. Flashcards can then reinforce compact information such as terminology, formulas, biological processes, historical evidence, and literary quotations.


The key distinction is between using notes to repair understanding and repeatedly rereading them for reassurance. Effective revision should move from explanation to retrieval as soon as accuracy permits.


### Topic-filtered questions and feedback


The[RevisionDojo Questionbank](https://www.revisiondojo.com/features/questionbank) lets students select a subject, paper, topic, level, and difficulty. It also provides worked reasoning, mark-scheme-style guidance, Jojo AI feedback, and topic-level accuracy tracking.


For example, an HL chemistry student who repeatedly loses marks on equilibrium calculations can isolate that topic, attempt a short set, classify each error, review the relevant concept, and try a parallel set later. Useful error categories include:


- Missing knowledge
- Misread command term
- Incorrect method
- Incomplete explanation
- Weak evidence or evaluation
- Careless execution
- Poor timing


A percentage indicates how the student performed. An error category identifies what must change next.


### Jojo AI as a connected tutor


Jojo AI is integrated with RevisionDojo's IB materials rather than functioning only as a blank general-purpose chatbot. Students can request explanations, generate targeted practice, review answers, and clarify feedback within the same study environment.


A productive prompt might ask Jojo AI to explain why a response missed a mark, compare it with the marking expectations, and create a similar question. Asking it simply to provide the answer removes the retrieval and decision-making the student needs to practise.


AI feedback should be treated as formative guidance, not an official grade. Teachers and IB examiners retain authority over assessment, while nuanced essays and coursework may require human judgment that automated systems cannot fully reproduce.


### Timed preparation and coursework support


RevisionDojo's[IB study features](https://www.revisiondojo.com/features) include Test Builder, Exam Mode, predicted papers, a mistakes log, essay marking, coursework exemplars, and criterion-level feedback tools. These resources serve different purposes.


Topic drills build accuracy, mixed tests develop switching and question selection, and full timed papers test pacing and stamina. Predicted papers provide additional current-syllabus practice, but no provider can reliably reveal the exact questions that will appear in an examination.


Coursework feedback can identify possible weaknesses in IA, EE, and TOK drafts. Students should use comments to revise their own reasoning and expression, then discuss important decisions with their teacher. No platform can guarantee the grade awarded to an externally moderated or examined submission.


### What the evidence does and does not show


RevisionDojo publishes testimonials from high-achieving students. On its[IB preparation platform](https://www.revisiondojo.com/) , Erik from Bromsgrove School describes balancing other commitments while scoring 45, while Rex also reports earning 45. Desen from Istanbul International School reports a 44 predicted grade and says categorized questions saved study time.


These experiences show that high-scoring students have used the platform. They do not establish that every top scorer uses it or that RevisionDojo alone produced their results.


RevisionDojo's[2026 State of Learning Survey](https://www.revisiondojo.com/research/state-of-learning-survey/2026) reports **2,975 completed responses** , comprising 2,887 students and 88 teachers across 1,224 schools. Among student respondents, **78.7%** reported that their average subject grade increased, with the average rising by 0.57 points from 4.82 to 5.39. Across 10,914 complete subject pairs, 48.5% showed improvement, 42.9% remained unchanged, and 8.6% declined.


The company-run survey is self-reported and observational. It does not establish that RevisionDojo caused the changes because participants were not randomly assigned to controlled groups. Teaching, tutoring, maturation, or increased effort may also have contributed, so the findings should be treated as encouraging reported outcomes rather than guaranteed results.


### A practical top-scorer workflow


Owning a strong resource has little value without a disciplined routine. Students can use RevisionDojo through this weekly cycle:


1. **Diagnose:** Attempt 8-12 questions from a current topic before extensive review.
2. **Classify:** Record each mistake as knowledge, interpretation, method, communication, or timing.
3. **Repair:** Use Study Notes, worked solutions, or Jojo AI to address the exact weakness.
4. **Retrieve:** Explain the concept from memory and review relevant Flashcards.
5. **Reattempt:** Complete new questions on the same skill after a delay.
6. **Integrate:** Combine the repaired topic with older material in a mixed set.
7. **Simulate:** Complete timed Exam Mode practice, increasing paper length near examinations.


For essay subjects, the cycle must include planning and writing rather than reading model responses alone. A student might draft one paragraph under time pressure, assess its claim, evidence, analysis, and evaluation, then rewrite the weakest component.


RevisionDojo's survey found that Questionbank was selected as impactful by **40.7%** of student respondents, Study Notes by **40.4%** , and Jojo AI chat by **35.7%** . These self-reported preferences do not prove effectiveness, but they reinforce the value students place on connecting explanation with active application.


### How parents should evaluate an IB platform


Parents should examine headline grade claims carefully. Ask who supplied the data, whether grades were independently verified, how many participants were included, and whether the evidence demonstrates correlation or causation.


The[RevisionDojo guide for parents choosing IB resources](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/best-resources-help-child-with-ib) emphasizes combining reliable explanations, active recall, exam-style practice, and feedback. Before paying, families should confirm that a platform covers the student's exact subjects and levels, explains lost marks, supports timed work, and sets honest limits around predicted papers and automated grading.


Parents can protect study time, help arrange mock conditions, and discuss patterns in the error log. They should avoid turning analytics into constant surveillance, which may encourage students to chase activity totals instead of confronting difficult material.


### Using AI without breaching IB academic integrity


The IB does not prohibit AI tools, but AI-generated material is not automatically the student's own work. Material from an AI tool included in submitted work must be acknowledged according to the school's requirements.


Jojo AI is best used as a tutor, question generator, and feedback source. It should not become a ghostwriter for an IA, EE, TOK essay, oral script, or other assessed component. Appropriate uses include requesting simpler explanations, generating practice questions, comparing methods, and identifying where an original response lacks detail.


Students must follow their school's current AI policy because schools may impose specific drafting, disclosure, and citation procedures. When uncertain, students should show their teacher how the tool was used before submitting work.


### Conclusion


The IB study platform top scorers need must connect accurate learning, retrieval, targeted questions, actionable feedback, delayed reattempts, timed papers, and criterion-aware coursework support.


RevisionDojo provides that structure through Study Notes, Flashcards, the Questionbank, Jojo AI, Exam Mode, predicted papers, and coursework tools. Its testimonials and survey findings are encouraging but do not guarantee improvement. Students should begin with the Questionbank and Study Notes, build an error-led routine, and add Jojo AI or Mock Exams when those tools address a specific study need.
